72.h: 68 - Yazīd ibn Abī Sufyān ibn Ḥarb ibn Umayyah al-Umawī * (ق)
72.t:
Ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy al-Umawī. ⟦1:328⟧
Brother of Muʿāwiyah on his father's side. He is called Yazīd the Good.
His mother was Zaynab bint Nawfal al-Kināniyyah, and he was the brother of the Mother of the Believers Umm Ḥabībah.
He was one of the wise and intelligent, and one of the renowned brave men. He accepted Islam on the day of the Conquest, and his Islam became good, and he witnessed Ḥunayn.
It is said that the Prophet ﷺ gave him from the spoils of Ḥunayn: one hundred camels and forty ounces of silver.
He was one of the four commanders whom Abū Bakr called upon to raid the Romans. Abū Bakr tied the banner for him and walked with him beside his mount, accompanying him, bidding him farewell and advising him, and that was only because of his nobility and the perfection of his religion. When Damascus was conquered, ʿUmar appointed him over it (1) .
He has a hadith on ablution narrated by Ibn Mājah (2) , and he has a narration from Abū Bakr.
Narrating from him: أبو عبد الله الأشعري، وجنادة بن أبي أمية.
He has a long biography in the History of the hadith master (الحافظ) Abū al-Qāsim.
The conquest of Caesarea (3) in Syria was at his hand.
ʿAwf al-Aʿrābī narrated from Muhājir Abū Mikhlad, who said:
حدثني أبو العالية، قال:
Yazīd ibn Abī Sufyān went on a raid with the people, and a precious slave girl fell to the share of a man, and Yazīd seized her by force.
Abū Dharr came to him and said: Return his slave girl to the man.
He hesitated, and he said: If ⟦1:329⟧ you do that, I have heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: (The first to change my Sunnah (السنة) will be a man of Banū Umayyah, called Yazīd).
He said: I adjure you by Allah, am I one of them?
He said: No.
So he returned the slave girl to the man (1) .
Al-Rūyānī transmitted it in his Musnad.
Ibrāhīm ibn Saʿd said: Yazīd ibn Abī Sufyān was over a quarter, Abū ʿUbaydah over a quarter, ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ over a quarter, and Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasanah over a quarter - meaning on the day of al-Yarmūk - and there was no commander over them that day.
Yazīd died in the plague, in the year 18. When he was dying, he appointed his brother Muʿāwiyah over his post, and ʿUmar confirmed him in that out of respect for Yazīd and to carry out his appointment.
In this year, in the plague, there also died (2) :
Abū ʿUbaydah, the trustworthy one of the community, Muʿādh ibn Jabal, master of the scholars, the commander and fighter in the cause of Allah Shuraḥbīl ibn Ḥasanah, ally of Banū Zuhrah, the cousin of the Prophet ﷺ al-Faḍl ibn al-ʿAbbās, who was in his twenties, al-Ḥārith ibn Hishām ibn al-Mughīrah al-Makhzūmī Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, one of the noble Companions (الصحابي) and brother of Abū Jahl, and Abū Jandal ibn Suhayl ibn ʿAmr al-ʿĀmirī (may Allah be pleased with them).

73.h: 69 - Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn al-Rabīʿ ibn ʿAbd al-ʿUzzā al-Qurashī *
73.t:
Ibn ʿAbd Shams ibn ʿAbd Manāf ibn Quṣayy ibn Kilāb al-Qurashī, ⟦1:330⟧ al-ʿAbshamī.
Son-in-law of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, husband of his daughter Zaynab, and father of Umāmah, whom the Prophet ﷺ used to carry in his prayer (1) .
His name was Laqīṭ.
It is said: his father's name was Rabīʿah, and he was the son of the sister of the Mother of the Believers Khadījah.
His mother was Hālah bint Khuwaylid, and Abū al-ʿĀṣ was called: the Cub of al-Baṭḥāʾ.
He accepted Islam five months before al-Ḥudaybiyah.
Al-Miswar ibn Makhramah said: The Prophet ﷺ praised Abū al-ʿĀṣ well for his in-law relationship.
He said: (He spoke to me and was truthful with me, and promised me and fulfilled it to me) (2) .
He had promised the Prophet ﷺ that he would return to Mecca after the battle of Badr and send his daughter Zaynab to him, and he fulfilled his promise and separated from her despite his great love for her. He was one of the merchants of Quraysh and their trustworthy men, and I know of no narration from him. ⟦1:331⟧
When he migrated, the Prophet ﷺ returned his wife Zaynab to him after six years on the basis of the first marriage (1) .
It came in one narration that he returned her to him with a new contract. When he was captured in the Badr affair, his wife had sent her necklace to ransom him with it.
The Prophet ﷺ said: (If you see fit to release her captive for her).
So the Companions (الصحابي) hastened to do that (2) .
And from the Sīrah: She sent in his ransom a necklace of hers which had belonged to Khadījah, who had given it to her at her wedding.
When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ saw it, he was moved with compassion for her and said: (If you see fit to release her captive for her and return it to her).
They said: Yes.
They released him, and the Prophet ﷺ took a pledge from him to let Zaynab go; she was among the weak women. The Prophet ﷺ asked him to keep that secret, and sent Zayd ⟦1:332⟧ ibn Ḥārithah and a man of the Anṣār.
He said: (Be in the valley of Yajaj (1) until Zaynab passes by you, and then accompany her).
That was a month after Badr. When Abū al-ʿĀṣ came to Mecca, he ordered her to join her father, and she made ready.
Her husband's brother Kinānah brought - I say: he was her maternal cousin - a camel, and she mounted. He took his bow and his quiver by day, and they went out in pursuit of her. Kinānah knelt down and scattered his quiver at Dhū Ṭuwā, and Habbār ibn al-Aswad frightened her with a spear.
Kinānah said: By Allah, no one will come near but I will put an arrow in him.
Abū Sufyān said: Man, hold back your arrows from us until we speak to you.
He held back, and Abū Sufyān stood before him and said:
You have not done well. You took the woman out in front of the people openly, and you know our misfortune and calamity and what has befallen us from Muḥammad, so people will think that this is out of a humiliation that struck us. By my life, we have no need of keeping her from her father. Take her back, and when the voices have died down and people have said that we returned her, then take her out secretly and join her to her father.
He said: He did so, and he took her out after some nights, and handed her over to Zayd and his companion, and they brought her.
Before the Conquest, Abū al-ʿĀṣ went out as a merchant to Syria with his wealth and much wealth of Quraysh. When he returned, a detachment met him and seized what he had, but he escaped them by fleeing. They came with what they had seized, and he came by night until he entered upon Zaynab, sought her protection, and she granted him protection.
When the Prophet ﷺ and the people were in the dawn prayer, Zaynab cried out from the women's section:
O people! I have granted protection to Abū al-ʿĀṣ ibn al-Rabīʿ.
The Prophet ﷺ sent to the detachment who had seized his wealth and said: (This man is of us, as you know, and you have seized wealth of his. If you are kind and return it, we love that, and if you refuse, it is the spoil of Allah, and you are more entitled to it).
They said: Rather we will return it.
They returned all of it, then he took it to Mecca and paid every owner of wealth his wealth, then said:
O company of Quraysh! Is ⟦1:333⟧ anything of yours still owed by me?
They said: No, and may Allah reward you well.
He said: Then I bear witness that there is no god but Allah and that Muḥammad is His servant and Messenger. By Allah, nothing prevented me from Islam with him except the fear that you would think I only wanted to consume your wealth.
Then he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.
On the authority of Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
The Prophet ﷺ returned Zaynab to him on the basis of the first marriage; he introduced nothing new.

74.t:
Zaynab, eldest of the daughters of the Messenger of Allah * ﷺ. This Zaynab (2) (may Allah be pleased with her) was the eldest of the daughters of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. She died in the year 8 of the Hijrah, and Umm ʿAṭiyyah washed her.
He gave them his waist-wrapper and said: (Wrap her in it) (3) . ⟦1:334⟧
The Prophet ﷺ loved her and praised her (may Allah be pleased with her).
She lived about thirty years.
Abū al-ʿĀṣ died in the month of Dhū al-Ḥijjah, in the year 12, in the caliphate (الخلافة) of al-Ṣiddīq.

75.t:
She whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to carry in his prayer (1) .
She is the daughter of his daughter. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib married her in the caliphate (الخلافة) of ʿUmar, and she remained with him for a time, and he had children by her.
She outlived him, until al-Mughīrah ibn Nawfal ibn al-Ḥārith ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib al-Hāshimī married her, and she died while with him after she had borne him Yaḥyā ibn al-Mughīrah.
She died in the reign of Muʿāwiyah ibn Abī Sufyān, and narrated nothing.

76.h: 72 - Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī Thābit ibn Zayd ibn Qays ibn Zayd **
76.t:
He was one of the great Companions (الصحابي), and one of those who memorised the entire Qurʾān in the time of the Prophet ﷺ. ⟦1:335⟧
Ibn Saʿd said: He is Thābit ibn Zayd ibn Qays ibn Zayd ibn al-Nuʿmān ibn Mālik ibn Thaʿlabah ibn Kaʿb ibn al-Khazraj ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj.
Abū Zayd the grammarian (النحوي), Saʿīd ibn Aws ibn Thābit ibn Bashīr ibn Abī Zayd al-Anṣārī, narrated to us about Thābit ibn Zayd. The grammarian (النحوي) said: He is my grandfather.
He witnessed Uḥud, and was one of the six who collected the Qurʾān. He settled in Basra and laid out a plot there, then came to Medina and died there.
ʿUmar stood at his grave and said:
May Allah have mercy on you, Abū Zayd! Today there has been buried the greatest of the people of the earth in trustworthiness (1) .
His son Bashīr was killed on the day of al-Ḥarrah (2) .
العقدي: حدثنا علي بن المبارك، عن الحسن أبي محمد، قال:
We entered upon Abū Zayd, whose leg had been struck on the day of Uḥud, and he gave the call to prayer and the second call sitting (3) .
It is said: the name of Abū Zayd was Aws.
It is said: Muʿādh, but the first is more correct. ⟦1:336⟧

77.h: 73 - ʿAbbād ibn Bishr ibn Waqsh ibn Zaghbah ibn Zaʿūrāʾ al-Anṣārī *
77.t:
Ibn ʿAbd al-Ashhal, the Imam (الإمام), Abū al-Rabīʿ al-Anṣārī (1) , al-Ashhalī.
One of the Badrīs (البدري), and one of the leaders of the Aws.
He lived forty-five years, and he is the one whose staff lit up for him on the night he returned to his house from the Messenger of Allah (2) ﷺ.
He accepted Islam at the hand of Muṣʿab ibn ʿUmayr, and was one of those who killed Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf the Jew (3) .
The Prophet ﷺ appointed him over the alms of Muzaynah and Banū Sulaym, and put him in charge of his guard in the expedition of Tabūk. He was of great standing (may Allah be pleased with him), fought well on the day of al-Yamāmah, and was one of the described brave men.
ابن إسحاق: عن يحيى بن عباد بن عبد الله (4) ، عن أبيه، قال:
ʿĀʾishah said: Three of the Anṣār, no one could count them as surpassing in merit, all of them from Banū ʿAbd al-Ashhal: Saʿd ibn Muʿādh, ʿAbbād ibn Bishr, and Usayd ibn ⟦1:337⟧ Ḥuḍayr (1) .
The Prophet ﷺ made a pact of brotherhood between him and Abū Ḥudhayfah ibn ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah.
It was narrated with a weak (ضعيف) chain of transmission (الإسناد) from Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī:
He heard ʿAbbād ibn Bishr say:
Tonight I saw as if the sky was opened for me, then closed over me, so it is - if Allah wills - martyrdom.
On the day of al-Yamāmah he looked and cried out: Break the scabbards of the swords! And he fought until he was killed with blows to his face (may Allah be pleased with him).
ابن إسحاق: عن محمد بن جعفر بن الزبير، عن عباد بن عبد الله بن الزبير، عن عائشة، قالت:
The Messenger of Allah ﷺ prayed at night in my house, and heard the voice of ʿAbbād ibn Bishr, and said: (O ʿĀʾishah! This is the voice of ʿAbbād ibn Bishr).
I said: Yes.
He said: (O Allah, forgive him (2)).
حماد بن سلمة: عن محمد بن إسحاق، عن حصين بن عبد الرحمن الخطمي، عن عبد الرحمن بن ثابت الأنصاري، عن عباد بن بشر:
That the Prophet ﷺ said: (O company of the Anṣār! You are the inner garment, and the people are the outer garment) (3) . ⟦1:338⟧
ʿAlī ibn (1) al-Madīnī said: I do not know of any other hadith for ʿAbbād.
ʿAbbād ibn Bishr ibn Qayẓī al-Ashhalī! Ibn al-Athīr said: There was confusion in the name of his grandfather.
He said: He is in fact ʿAbbād ibn Bishr ibn Waqsh ibn Zaghbah ibn Zaʿūrāʾ ibn ʿAbd al-Ashhal ibn Jusham ibn al-Ḥārith ibn al-Khazraj ibn al-Aws al-Awsī.
He was martyred (may Allah be pleased with him) on the day of al-Yamāmah.
As for ʿAbbād ibn Bishr ibn Qayẓī; he is an Anṣārī of Banū Ḥārithah who led his people in prayer in the time of the Prophet ﷺ.
He has a hadith on turning around in prayer toward the Kaʿbah (2) , and Allah knows best.
ʿAbbād ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Zubayr said: My father named me ʿAbbād only after him (3) - meaning the Ashhalī -.
And among his poetry:
I called out to him, but he did not respond to my voice ... and he came forth appearing from the top of a wall
I went back to him, and he said: Who is calling? ... I said: Your brother ʿAbbād ibn Bishr ⟦1:339⟧
And here is our coat of mail, pledged, so take it ... for a month - if he fulfils - or half a month
He said: A company who went hungry and starved ... yet were not deprived of wealth, without being poor
He came toward us hastening quickly ... and said to us: You have come for a matter
And in our right hands are sharp white swords ... tried, with which I scatter the unbelievers
Ibn Maslamah embraced him, the one by whom unbelievers are destroyed ... like a fierce lion
And he charged at him with his drawn sword ... and Abū ʿAbs ibn Jabr laid him low (1)
And Allah was our sixth, and we returned ... with the most blessed favour and the mightiest victory (2)
ʿAbbād has one hadith, which has preceded, and it is by Ibn Isḥāq: عن حصين بن عبد الرحمن الأنصاري، عن عبد الرحمن بن ثابت بن الصامت، عن عباد بن بشر:
That the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: (O company of the Anṣār! You are the inner garment, and the people are the outer garment, so let me not be attacked from your side) (3) .
